title: First Combinations
statement: Implement `solve(items, k)`. Return the first `k` unordered pairs of distinct items, in the order combinations() would yield them: earlier items are chosen first, and the second index increases before the first moves. If `k` is larger than the number of pairs, return all pairs. `k` of 0 returns an empty list. Items are strings.
constraints: Pairs are lists of two strings
Do not repeat a pair in reverse
hints: islice avoids building the rest when k is small. Slicing a full list is acceptable for these sizes.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: combinations yields each unordered pair once.

editorial: combinations yields each unordered pair once. Generating every pair and then slicing is fine when the input is small. islice stops early when k is small and the input is large. The order is lexicographic on the positions, not on a sort of the values.
